intro.source: 6 questions about Lessons 7–9. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 6 questions about Lessons 7–9. No need to rush. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you want.

questions.0.question.source: What happened in Singapore on 15 February 1942?
questions.0.question.back: What happened in Singapore on 15 February 1942?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: The occupation came to an end.

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The occupation ended in 1945. On 15 February 1942, it began. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The occupation ended in 1945. On 15 February 1942, the occupation began. Look back at Lesson 7.

questions.0.options.1.text.back: Japanese lessons were stopped in schools.

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. In 1942, Japanese lessons became compulsory in schools. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. In 1942, Japanese lessons became compulsory in schools. Look back at Lesson 7.

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. British forces gave up at the Ford Factory. Then the occupation began. It lasted until 1945.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. British forces gave up at the Ford Factory. Then the occupation began. The occupation lasted until 1945.

questions.1.question.source: You want to learn what people in Singapore ate in 1943. Which source would help most?
questions.1.question.back: You want to know what people in Singapore ate in 1943. Which source helps most?

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Lee Geok Boi used oral history interviews to write about food in this time. Memories can tell us about meals.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. Lee Geok Boi used oral history interviews to write about food at this time. Memories can tell us about daily meals.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: A 2025 photo of the Former Ford Factory
questions.1.options.1.text.back: A photo of the Former Ford Factory from 2025

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The photo shows the building in 2025. It cannot show what people ate in 1943. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The photo shows the building in 2025. The photo cannot show what people ate in 1943. Look back at Lesson 7.

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. That rule tells us about school lessons, not meals. Look back at Lesson 7.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. That rule tells us about lessons at school, not daily meals. Look back at Lesson 7.

questions.2.question.source: On 17 August 1945, two leaders said in public that Indonesia was free. What is this kind of statement called?
questions.2.question.back: On 17 August 1945, two leaders said openly that Indonesia was already free. What is the name of this kind of statement?

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A proclamation is a statement made to all. In Indonesia, people mark 17 August as the day they became free.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. A proclamation is a statement made to everyone. In Indonesia, people mark 17 August as the day they became free.

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. The Netherlands handed over power later, in 1949. That came after the proclamation. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. The Netherlands handed over power later, in 1949. That event happened after the proclamation. Look back at Lesson 8.

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. A federation is a group of states joined under one main government. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. A federation is a group of states joined under one main government. Look back at Lesson 8.

questions.3.question.source: A student says that Malaysia became free on 31 August 1957. What needs to change?
questions.3.question.back: A learner says Malaysia became free on 31 August 1957. What needs to be changed?

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. 17 August 1945 is the date of Indonesia's proclamation. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. 17 August 1945 is the date of Indonesia's proclamation. Look back at Lesson 8.

questions.3.options.1.text.source: Change Malaysia to the Federation of Malaya
questions.3.options.1.text.back: Change Malaysia to the Federation of Malaya

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. It was the Federation of Malaya that became free in 1957. Malaysia was formed later, in 1963.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. It was the Federation of Malaya that became free in 1957. Malaysia was formed later, in 1963.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. In 1956, leaders signed an agreement in London. It set the day of independence in 1957. Look back at Lesson 8.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. In 1956, the leaders signed an agreement in London. That agreement set the day of independence in 1957. Look back at Lesson 8.

questions.4.question.source: In March 2000, a UN report said many schools in Timor-Leste had been repaired. What does this date tell you?
questions.4.question.back: In March 2000, a UN report stated many schools in Timor-Leste had been repaired. What does this date tell you?

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The report is from 2000. That is before independence was restored in 2002. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The report is from 2000. That is before independence was restored in 2002. Look back at Lesson 9.

questions.4.options.1.text.back: Repairs began during the transition period

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. Work on schools began before 2002, while a UN team ran the country with East Timorese leaders.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. Work on repairing schools began before 2002, while a UN team ran the country together with East Timorese leaders.

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. 2024 is the date of the school photo. Repairs began much earlier. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. 2024 is the date of the school photo. Repairs began much earlier. Look back at Lesson 9.

questions.5.stimulus.title.source: A made-up school in a made-up town
questions.5.stimulus.title.back: A made-up school in a made-up town

questions.5.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. The made-up town of Lorvan has a new school building with a strong roof. But there are very few books. Most teachers have had no training. Many children do not understand the language used in class.
questions.5.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. The made-up town of Lorvan has a new school building with a strong roof. But there are very few books. Most teachers have never had training. Many children do not understand the language used in class.

questions.5.question.source: What would help the children in Lorvan learn the most?
questions.5.question.back: What would help the children in Lorvan learn the most?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: New paint on the school walls
questions.5.options.0.text.back: New paint on the school walls

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The building is already fixed. A school needs more than walls. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The building is already repaired. A school needs more than walls. Look back at Lesson 9.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: A big party to open the school
questions.5.options.1.text.back: A big ceremony to open the school

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A party lasts one day. Learning needs teachers, books and a language children know. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A ceremony lasts only one day. Learning needs teachers, books and a language children understand. Look back at Lesson 9.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.note: "party" rendered "majlis" (a celebration/function), the natural Malaysian word for an opening party.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: Teachers, books and a known language
questions.5.options.2.text.back: Teachers, books and a language that is understood

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. In Timor-Leste, too, buildings were fixed first. Teachers, books and language are also needed for learning.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. In Timor-Leste too, buildings were repaired first. Teachers, books and language are also needed for learning.
